name: Bohrium

discovery.discoverer: Peter Armbruster & Gottfried Münzenberg, GSI Darmstadt

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom, decaying within seconds.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; only ever produced and observed as single atoms.
notableCharacteristics: Named after physicist Niels Bohr, whose atomic model laid the groundwork for understanding electron shell structure across the entire periodic table.
whyHere: Predicted to sit in Group 7 alongside manganese and rhenium, bohrium's expected +7 oxidation state chemistry follows the group trend, though only a handful of individual atoms have ever been chemically studied to test it.
didYouKnow: Discovering and confirming bohrium required detecting a decay chain from a single atom that survives for only a fraction of a second before splitting apart — a level of experimental precision Niels Bohr himself never had access to.
genZNote: Named after the guy whose atomic model you learn in high school, now representing an element nobody's ever seen more than one atom of at once.
